problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that $u$ and $v$ are orthogonal. Find $(2u+3w)\cdot v+u\cdot (v-w).$

feedback.problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 5 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ be vectors such that $u\,⊥\,v.$ Find $(v+w)\cdot u+v\cdot (u+w).$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $u$ and $v$ are orthogonal vectors, we have that $u\cdot v=0.$ Therefore, using linearity of the dot product to expand the parentheses, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(v+w)\cdot u+v\cdot (u+w) & =v\cdot u+w\cdot u+v\cdot u+v\cdot w \\  & =0+w\cdot u+0+v\cdot w \\  & =w\cdot u+v\cdot w \\  & =((-3)\cdot 3+2\cdot (-2)+5\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot (-2)) \\  & +(2\cdot (-3)+4\cdot 2+0\cdot 5+(-1)\cdot (-2)) \\  & =(-9-4+5+4)+(-6+8+0+2) \\  & =-4+4 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
